lines: ANBTX reported $5.5 billion in total assets as of September 30, 2025, ranking it 19th among all banks headquartered in Texas by asset size — a milestone that places it firmly within the mid-tier community bank segment ($5–10B) while positioning it well ahead of its early-2000s scale of approximately $2 billion. The bank operates 28+ banking centers across eight Texas counties (Collin, Dallas, Hunt, Johnson, Kaufman, Rockwall, Tarrant, and Van Zandt), supplemented by two specialized loan production offices serving the South Dallas and Frisco markets. [E-020, E-010]

The bank's asset base has compounded at approximately 8.9% CAGR since 1999 (when the Bank of Van Zandt acquisition brought assets to approximately $650 million), reflecting a strategy of disciplined acquisition activity through 2018 followed by sustained organic growth. Post-2018 organic CAGR is estimated at approximately 3.5% annually — consistent with a community bank deepening its North Texas market penetration rather than expanding geographically. Revenue is estimated at approximately $240 million on a net interest margin-driven model typical of community banking institutions in this asset range. [E-020]

Workforce scale stands at approximately 750–760 employees based on the most recent technographic intelligence, consistent with a banking institution of this asset size. ANBTX's 16-time recognition as a Top Workplaces DFW honoree by The Dallas Morning News (2009, 2011–2025, 16 total) — including its most recent recognition in the large company category in 2025 — signals sustained employee engagement metrics that reduce talent acquisition costs and support customer-facing service quality. [E-016, E-038]

Two strategic subsidiaries extend ANBTX's revenue diversification beyond core banking: ANBTX Insurance Services Inc. (operating as Sleeper, Sewell & Company, acquired 2006) provides personal insurance, commercial insurance, group and individual health coverage, and risk management services through a Dallas-based office; and ANBTX Wealth Management offers asset management, financial planning, investment advisory, and trust and estate planning services, leveraging an Ameriprise Financial platform integration implemented in 2022. [E-020, E-035]

ANBTX's asset trajectory over 26 years reflects a consistent compounding of acquisition-led and organic growth. From approximately $650 million at year-end 1999 (post-Bank of Van Zandt acquisition) to $5.5 billion as of September 2025, the bank has grown at an estimated 8.9% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) — a rate that places it among the more consistent growers in the Texas community banking sector. The post-2018 period, during which ANBTX completed its last acquisition (G-6 Corporation / First State Bank in Mesquite), marks a deliberate shift to organic growth and technology-led scale expansion. [E-020]

Post-2018 organic asset CAGR is estimated at approximately 3.5% annually, consistent with disciplined net interest margin management in a competitive Texas banking market. Revenue is estimated at approximately $240 million — reflecting a classic community banking model where net interest income from loans and deposits constitutes the primary revenue stream, supplemented by fee income from treasury management, wealth management, insurance services, and mortgage origination. The January 2026 addition of seven commercial banking associates — under Chief Strategy Officer Steve White's C&I diversification mandate — signals that the loan book expansion strategy is accelerating into 2026. [E-002, E-016]

Financial trend classification: STABLE-GROWING. ANBTX has delivered consistent year-over-year asset growth without material contraction periods. Its 19th-largest Texas bank ranking as of September 2025 represents a gain from prior-year positions, confirming continued relative growth within the Texas banking sector. As the bank approaches the $7–8B range over the next 3–5 years, the $10B regulatory threshold — at which CFPB direct supervision, enhanced Durbin Amendment provisions, and full DFAST stress testing apply — will become a strategic planning driver that meaningfully increases technology and compliance investment requirements. [E-020, E-010]

firmographics.narrative_md:
Comprehensive organizational context. Every claim is linked to evidence IDs. Financial data is sourced from the most recent available Statement of Condition, OCC regulatory filings, and technographic intelligence sources.

American National Bank of Texas (ANBTX) traces its origins to November 22, 1875, when Waters, Bivins & Corley Bank opened in Terrell, Texas — making it one of the oldest independently operated financial institutions in the state. The bank has operated continuously under federal charter since July 1, 1981, when the current commercial bank charter (OCC Charter No. 17043) was established. The institution's current legal name was adopted in 1995, when it transitioned from American National Bank of Terrell — its identity since 1903 — to reflect its expanded North Texas footprint. [E-010, E-020]

ANBTX is independently owned and privately held, a structural characteristic that has defined its strategy across multiple leadership generations. Robert A. Hulsey has served as President & Chief Executive Officer since 1989 — a 37-year tenure that has presided over the bank's growth from a sub-$200M community institution to a $5.5B North Texas banking enterprise. Hulsey's long tenure signals continuity, deep local market knowledge, and a deliberate resistance to acquisition by larger regional or national banks — a governance stance reinforced by ANBTX's consistent independence messaging: 'Your Bank for Life,' 'EmpoweringPossible,' and 'Making communities stronger by making businesses stronger.' [E-020, E-035]

The board of directors reflects ANBTX's dual mandate of community heritage and forward-looking innovation. The 2023 appointment of Dennis Cail (co-founder and CEO of Zirtue, an AI-first relationship-based lending fintech) and Suzanne Cruz-Sewell (Assistant Vice President of Business Diversity at DFW International Airport) signals deliberate infusion of AI competency and diversity strategy at the highest governance level. Robert Messer (SEVP & CFO) serves concurrently as Chairman of the Risk Management Association (RMA) Community Bank Council and as a board member — providing ANBTX direct access to industry-leading risk management intelligence and peer benchmarking. [E-035, E-015]

ANBTX is supervised by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) as a federally chartered national bank, subject to OCC examination cycles of 12–18 months. The bank is a member of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) with all deposits backed by the full faith and credit of the U.S. Government. ANBTX's federal charter, combined with its OCC supervisory relationship, means its compliance obligations span the full FFIEC examination framework — including IT, cybersecurity, BSA/AML, consumer protection, and third-party risk management. [E-010]
